aria: Animated recap of the Hawks' 124 to 121 home win over Brooklyn: Nickeil Alexander-Walker's go-ahead free throw with 1:26 left, quarter-by-quarter scoring, Jalen Johnson's 30 points, the top scorers, how the Hawks won, and the next game against the Lakers.
notes: Box score from the Hawks' 124–121 home win over the Brooklyn Nets on Nov 7, 2026, from Covers.com's full box score and Plain Text Sports (they agree on every player line), with game details from the AP (via Yahoo Sports, WRAL and Atlanta News First), Reuters/Field Level Media and Yahoo Sports. All 124 Hawks points and all 121 Nets points are accounted for. Points in the paint (70–48) and fast-break points (20–4) are in both box scores; points off turnovers (28–13) are from Plain Text Sports and match Nets coach Jordi Fernandez's '22 turnovers for 28 points'. The league stats feed wasn't available for this recap; records and the conference standing come from the site's standings after Saturday (FOX Sports' conference table).

Biggest leads: Brooklyn's 17 (31–14 in the first quarter, per the AP, Field Level Media and Plain Text Sports' play-by-play) and Atlanta's 7 (123–116 with 9.5 seconds left). Atlanta trailed until the final 1:26.

The play of the game is an original illustration of Nickeil Alexander-Walker's free throws with 1:26 left, after he was fouled by Mikel Brown Jr.: the first tied it 114–114 and the second gave the Hawks a 115–114 lead, their first of the night (AP; Field Level Media; Plain Text Sports' play-by-play). He added a running layup at 1:07 for 117–114, and Jalen Johnson's three-point play with 38.5 seconds left made it 120–114. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Atlanta Hawks or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The shooter in the play of the game is drawn to Alexander-Walker’s listed 6-foot-5 and 205 pounds (Basketball-Reference, Wikipedia), with arms scaled to his reported 6-foot-9½ wingspan (Bleacher Report's 2019 draft scouting report); his No. 7 is from Wikipedia. It is an original silhouette with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
